title: SQL Syllabus (Curriculum)
role: Beginner-friendly coverage checklist and sequencing reference for core SQL syntax, querying, joins, DML, DDL, constraints, views, and security basics.

title: SQL Tutorial
role: Supplementary examples and exercises for foundational SQL statements; used as a breadth reference rather than the authority for engine-specific behavior.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Tutorial
role: Primary semantic reference for relational concepts, querying, joins, aggregates, updates, deletes, views, foreign keys, transactions, and window functions.

title: PostgreSQL 18 — Queries
role: Detailed reference for FROM/WHERE/GROUP BY/HAVING, set operations, sorting, LIMIT/OFFSET, CTEs, recursive queries, and query processing.

title: PostgreSQL 18 — Data Definition
role: Reference for tables, defaults, generated columns, constraints, privileges, schemas, inheritance/partitioning concepts, and other DDL topics.

title: PostgreSQL 18 — Transactions
role: Primary reference for atomic transactions, BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, savepoints, and transaction reasoning.

title: PostgreSQL 18 — Window Functions
role: Primary reference for OVER, PARTITION BY, window ordering, ranking, running calculations, and the difference between windows and aggregation.

title: SQLite — SELECT
role: Runtime-aligned reference for SELECT grammar and behavior in the in-browser SQLite practice environment.

title: SQLite — Transaction
role: Runtime-aligned reference for SQLite transaction behavior and explicit transaction control.

title: SQLite Query Planning
role: Accessible explanation of indexes, lookup strategies, multi-column indexes, covering indexes, and query planning trade-offs.

title: SQLBolt Interactive SQL Lessons
role: Practice-sequencing reference: short concept blocks followed immediately by hands-on SELECT, filtering, joins, aggregates, DML, and DDL exercises.

title: SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
role: Security authority for parameterized queries/prepared statements, allow-list validation, and why string-concatenated SQL is unsafe.
